reason: Both conversations asked the same sensible first question (new/cleaned vs electrical-type smell), both correctly recognised the hot-plastic smell from behind/below as an electrical fire risk, and both told the homeowner to stop using it and get an engineer before any further use. Conversation 1 issued a stop banner earlier but muddled it by saying the smell 'can be normal' in the same breath, deferred isolation to the engineer in its final turn, and was slightly over-confident naming the terminal block as 'the most likely cause'; Conversation 2 waited one turn to escalate but then gave a clean, explicit 'switch off at the cooker isolator or consumer unit' instruction and hedged between terminal block and internal wiring. Neither probed the cooker switch, flicker or crackle, nor distinguished electrician from appliance engineer, so the net result is essentially equivalent.
